clue.text: Being discharged and so deteriorating

definitions.meaning: first meaning: firing, as a gun or an alarm does
second meaning: turning bad, as milk or meat does

explanation.surface: A patient sent home from hospital who promptly takes a turn for the worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both a firearm firing and food spoiling, so one phrase serves both senses.

clue.text: Aristocrats demanding information before trial

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a try is an attempt or trial

explanation.surface: Nobles insisting on being told the facts before a court case begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the well-born landed class, close to the aristocracy, so they fit as a loose synonym.

clue.text: A1 band playing in a Nigerian city

indicators.note: a band playing performs, so its letters are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: A and the digit 1 read as the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A first-rate group performing a gig in Nigeria.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class; its digit stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is a large city in south-western Nigeria, so it is an example of a Nigerian city.

clue.text: Local news broadcaster

definitions.meaning: first meaning: neighbourhood talk and rumour
second meaning: a person who spreads that talk around

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a local radio station; the broadcaster is a person who spreads rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both idle talk about neighbours and the person who passes such talk on.

clue.text: Bars for everybody in the woods

parts.note: a forest is woodland
read as all's, belonging to everybody

explanation.surface: Pubs open to everyone, out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: the woods give FOREST, and 'for everybody' is taken as all's. 'Bars' looks like a noun for pubs; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall something is to prevent it by acting first, so it is a synonym for bars in the sense of blocks.

clue.text: Put bun-mix on lip and relax

indicators.note: to mix things is to stir them together, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled
a lip is an edge or extremity, loosely an end

explanation.surface: A cook's odd instruction to smear a bun mixture on someone's lip, then take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lip for END is a loose equivalence: both name the outer edge of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbend is to loosen up and stop being stiff or formal, which is a synonym for relaxing.

clue.text: Another would complete the score

parts.note: surface reading: one more goal or run would settle a game's result
setter's reading: a score is twenty, so the number one short of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests a sports result; it is the old word for twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding one more to this number makes twenty, which is what a score means as a count.

clue.text: The elder representing the monarch in years gone by

definitions.text: the monarch in years gone by

indicators.note: representing something means portraying it in another form, so those letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior figure standing in for the sovereign in olden days.
explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred was the name of Anglo-Saxon English kings, most famously Ethelred the Unready.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred ruled England over a thousand years ago, so he is an example of a monarch from the distant past.

clue.text: King of the underworld having lock trouble

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Pluto struggling with a jammed lock on the gates of Hades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is suffering or difficulty, a synonym for trouble as a noun.

clue.text: A beastly boat!

parts.note: surface reading: a nasty, unpleasant vessel
setter's reading: a vessel full of beasts, the animals taken aboard two by two

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' usually means horrid; here it means literally carrying beasts, which points to the biblical vessel of the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch built a vessel to carry pairs of every animal through the Flood, so it is the boat of beasts.

clue.text: In the main Cheshire moves slowly

indicators.note: something in the following words sits within them, so the answer lies inside the run of letters that comes next

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of main into the start of Cheshire

explanation.surface: Something in the sea off Cheshire, an English county, creeping along; 'the main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'at sea' or 'mostly'; 'In' is the signal that the answer is tucked inside the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to advance by tiny amounts, a verb for creeping forward slowly.

clue.text: Most willing to study — that is a virtuous person

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
St is the abbreviation for saint, a virtuous person

explanation.surface: A pupil most eager to study is held up as a model of virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready can mean prepared and willing, so the superlative is a synonym for most willing.

clue.text: Older animals hold the Spanish back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the combined letters are read from right to left
to hold something is to have it inside you, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: rats are animals
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Elderly beasts holding back a group of Spaniards.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes just after the first letter, and the reversal applies to the whole combined word, not just the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale means no longer fresh, past its best, so staler is a looser synonym for older, as of bread.

clue.text: Striving to study nursing

parts.note: to con is to study carefully
tending the sick is nursing them

explanation.surface: Working hard to qualify in nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: Contending means competing or struggling against difficulty, a synonym for striving.

clue.text: Their rise and fall may well be of interest to outgoing people

definitions.text: Their rise and fall may well be of interest to outgoing people

parts.words: Their rise and fall may well be of interest to outgoing people
parts.note: surface reading: sociable, extrovert types following someone's career or fortunes
setter's reading: people about to go out of doors, checking the instrument whose reading rises and falls with the weather

explanation.walkthrough: 'Outgoing' looks like 'extrovert'; it means literally going out, and such people watch the weather glass before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: These instruments measure air pressure, whose rise or fall forecasts fine or wet weather for anyone heading outside.

clue.text: The strength of the current

parts.note: surface reading: how powerfully a river or tide is flowing
setter's reading: an electric current, whose strength is measured in amps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests water; it is electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical current is measured in amperes, so the measure of its flow is named after that unit.

clue.text: Cartoonist converting a manor, it appears

indicators.note: converting changes one thing into another, so the letters are rebuilt into a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cartoonist seemingly turning a stately home into something else, perhaps flats.
explanation.definitionFit: An animator draws the frames of animated cartoons, so the job is a kind of cartoonist.

clue.text: Seeing a drug cutting pain

indicators.note: a thing cutting another goes into it, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Seeing a painkiller cut down someone's suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' simply goes with drug: a drug, namely pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting means catching sight of something, a synonym for seeing.

clue.text: A fellow turning up after one — late for work

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the word beside it is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man turns up after one o'clock, late for his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reads as arriving; 'turning' reverses up. 'After one' places that reversal after I, though MAN still comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To manipulate is to handle or operate something skilfully, as in working a lever, a synonym for work.

clue.text: Soldiers with money? — That's new!

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a cent is a unit of money

explanation.surface: Soldiers being paid is a novelty, someone remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are the British Army's corps of military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent means having happened lately, a synonym for new.

clue.text: Flier casting a vote about to go in

indicators.note: something told to go in is placed inside another, so one piece is set within the rest
casting can mean shaping in a mould, so the letters are formed anew

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled
c. is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A pilot casting a ballot about to go into the polling booth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with an upcurved bill, so it is an example of a flier.

clue.text: Even America can raise the wind

parts.note: flat means level, even
abbreviation of the United States

explanation.surface: A boast that even Americans can whip up a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise the wind' is an idiom for raising money; here it is gas in the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatus is the medical term for gas in the digestive tract, the bodily sense of wind.

clue.text: Taking quarters with German may end discord

parts.note: east and north are two compass quarters
mit is German for with

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word may

explanation.surface: Taking lodgings with a German might put an end to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May end' looks like 'might finish'; it is the last letter of may. 'With German' asks for the German word for with.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility between people, so it is a near synonym for discord or strife.

clue.text: New form of travel in space

indicators.note: a new form is a remodelling, so the following letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new way of getting about in outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space' looks like the cosmos of space travel; here it means a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a gap between two points in time or position, a synonym for space.

clue.text: An order given in Northern Ireland

definitions.note: the answer is a place in Northern Ireland

parts.note: taken as written
trim means neat order, as in good trim

explanation.surface: A command handed out in Belfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pointer to a place: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is a county and town of Northern Ireland, so it is an example of a place located there.

clue.text: The little beast makes many a doctor act strangely

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

indicators.note: doing something strangely means in an odd, irregular way, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: a means one, written as the Roman numeral
a vet is an animal doctor
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A small pest that drives many a doctor to behave oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'many' and 'a' are numbers here: C for a hundred and I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The civet is a small cat-like mammal of Africa and Asia, so it fits as an example of a little wild animal.

clue.text: Some points about waste material cause much ill feeling

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the points are placed around the material

parts.note: east, north and east are compass points
a rag is a scrap of waste cloth

explanation.surface: Arguments over rubbish that stir up bad blood between neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage someone is to make them furious, a verb for provoking strong anger.

clue.text: In a stage presentation it creates quite a stir

indicators.note: a presentation is a staging or arrangement, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatrical show that causes a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like the subject of the sentence but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or shake, both literally and in rousing public feeling.
